short: Remade the presidency as a popular office, and drove the southeastern nations west.
full:
Jackson arrived in 1829 having lost the 1824 election in the House despite leading the popular vote. He claimed a direct mandate from the electorate that no predecessor had asserted, used the veto twelve times, more than all six previous presidents combined, and filled offices with supporters in what critics named the spoils system.

His war on the Second Bank of the United States ended with a veto of its recharter in 1832 and the removal of federal deposits, contributing to the panic that broke soon after he left. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 authorised the expulsion of the Cherokee, Choctaw, Creek, Chickasaw and Seminole from their lands; the Cherokee were marched west in 1838 on the Trail of Tears, with thousands dying. When South Carolina tried to nullify the tariff in 1832 he threatened force, and the state gave way.
